claims.text: A thin, uniform Ni interlayer can be deposited on W particles by vapor deposition before Cu infiltration and sintering.
A Ni interlayer on W particles will improve the wettability of W by Cu.
A Ni interlayer will improve interfacial adhesion between W and Cu.
Improved wettability and adhesion will promote intimate contact between W and Cu.
Improved W–Cu contact will minimize voids and defects at phase boundaries.
Ni acts as a wetting agent by reducing the surface-energy mismatch between molten Cu and W.
Reducing the surface-energy mismatch will produce a more uniform W–Cu microstructure during sintering.
The Ni interlayer will limit phase separation during processing.
Reduced voiding and phase separation will improve the thermal conductivity of the W–Cu composite.
The Ni-mediated interface and more uniform microstructure will improve mechanical strength under irradiation.
Compared with an otherwise comparable uncoated W–Cu composite, the Ni-coated composite will contain fewer interfacial voids.
Compared with the uncoated baseline, the Ni-coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity.
Compared with the uncoated baseline, the Ni-coated composite will have greater mechanical durability during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Spark-plasma-sintered, vapor-coated, or mechanically alloyed W–Cu composites without an interlayer are prone to void formation and phase separation.
The proposed composite is intended to retain its benefits under thermal loads and irradiation typical of fusion-reactor joints.
